title: Write a check that finds a faulty count
prompt: A candidate method takes a `List<int>` and should return how many of its items are greater than 0. Write `public static bool CountCheck(Func<List<int>, int> candidate)`. Return true when the candidate behaves correctly on the inputs you choose, and false when it does not. Your check must return false for a faulty candidate that also counts zeros, and for one that counts every item.
hints: Which items would a faulty candidate count that a correct one does not?
A list with only positive numbers gives the same answer for all three candidates. Include a 0 and a negative number.
Call candidate with a list such as 3, 0, -2, 5 and compare the result with 2, the correct count.
checkLabels: A correct candidate must pass your check.
A candidate that also counts zeros must fail your check.
A candidate that counts every item must fail your check.

wrongAnswers.misconception: Tests only positive numbers, which every candidate counts the same way.
Writes down the wrong expected count, so correct code fails.

feedback: A check needs an input where correct and faulty code give different answers, and the expected value must come from the rule, worked out by hand.
